title: Psychology

sourceText.admission:
Admission Requirements

• Minimum 2.00 cumulative UW GPA

• Completion of one of the following math courses with a minimum 2.0 grade: MATH 111, MATH 112, MATH 120, or MATH 124.

• Completion of the following psychology courses with a minimum 2.0 grade in each course and a cumulative 2.50 GPA in the three courses: PSYCH 101, PSYCH 202, and PSYCH 209.

• Admission is competitive based on the following criteria: 

• Preparation for a major in psychology as indicated by the grades earned in courses required for admission

• GPA, with an emphasis on grades earned in psychology courses

• Other evidence of a commitment to becoming a psychology major

• Personal statement reflecting an interest in and commitment to becoming a psychology major

• Copies of unofficial transcripts from all schools attended (UW and transfer).

Meeting the above criteria does not guarantee admission to the department.

• The application deadline is the first Friday of autumn, winter, and spring quarters; no applications are accepted summer quarter. Applications and additional information are available in 119A Guthrie.

sections.credentialOverview:
Credential Overview

The BS program emphasizes current research and theory and stresses scientific and statistical reasoning skills through coursework and active participation in research.
sections.credentialCompletionRequirements:
Completion Requirements

84-86 credits

• PSYCH 101, PSYCH 202, PSYCH 209 (minimum grade of 2.5), PSYCH 317 and PSYCH 318

• One laboratory course from PSYCH 330, PSYCH 331, PSYCH 332, PSYCH 334, PSYCH 335, or PSYCH 419

• One course from PSYCH 300, PSYCH 302, PSYCH 333, or PSYCH 355

• One course from PSYCH 303, PSYCH 305, PSYCH 306, PSYCH 345, or PSYCH 357/GWSS 357

• One additional course from PSYCH 300, PSYCH 302, PSYCH 303, PSYCH 305, PSYCH 306, PSYCH 333, PSYCH 345, PSYCH 355, or PSYCH 357/GWSS 357

• Three additional graded upper-division PSYCH courses with at least two courses at the 400-level (cannot include PSYCH 491 through PSYCH 499) (9 to 15 credits)

• PSYCH 499 (3 credits)

• PSYCH 496, PSYCH 497, or PSYCH 498 (3 credits) or 3 additional credits of PSYCH 499

• Up to 6 credits in 200- to 400-level PSYCH elective courses to reach a minimum 66 psychology credits

• Students may not use PSYCH 200 as an elective if PSYCH 300 is used to fulfill major requirements; or use PSYCH 203 as an elective if PSYCH 303 is used to fulfill major requirements; or use PSYCH 206 as an elective if PSYCH 306 is used to fulfill major requirements; or use PSYCH 245 as an elective if PSYCH 345 is used to fulfill major requirements.

• Courses in related fields (18-20 credits): 

• MATH 124. While not a major requirement, some students may choose to take MATH 120 first in order to feel prepared for MATH 124.

• One 5 credit biological science course from BIOL 118, BIOL 161, BIOL 162, BIOL 180, BIOL 200, or BIOL 220

• One of the following philosophy courses: PHIL 120, PHIL 160

• One social science course (3 to 5 credits) from anthropology or sociology

• Minimum 2.50 cumulative GPA in all PSYCH courses applied toward the degree (UW and transfer), with a minimum 2.0 grade in each course presented for the major. Note that a grade of 2.5 or higher is required in PSYCH 209 in order for students to progress to the PSYCH 317/PSYCH 318 statistics series.

• Transfer students must meet all of the above requirements and are required to complete at least 15 graded credits in psychology at the 300- and 400-level through the UW.
